candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: L33718 is the PAP device policy that directly covers E0601 CPAP for obstructive sleep apnea. Its initial coverage criteria A-C (in-person clinical evaluation before the sleep test, a qualifying sleep test, and related requirements) match this patient: a Type I polysomnography showed AHI 14 events/hour with SpO2 nadir 81%, and the in-person evaluation preceded the study. The policy governs the E0601 order for this OSA diagnosis, while L33405 and L36902 cover sleep testing and sleep study criteria rather than the device itself.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: On 2026-03-12 Dr. Irene779 Kirlin939 saw the patient in person for evaluation of possible obstructive sleep apnea (R152, encounter R49). The attended in-laboratory polysomnography was performed on 2026-03-23 (R50), after that evaluation.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test (as defined below) that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of: a. Excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia; or b. Hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: Alternative 1 is not met because the AHI is 14 events/hour, below 15. Alternative 2 applies: the AHI of 14 is within 5 to 14, and 91 total events over 6.5 hours of sleep (R139, R143) exceeds the minimum of 10. Documentation of excessive daytime sleepiness is present: Epworth Sleepiness Scale score of 17 (R102) and reported dozing off while reading and watching television (R152). The history of myocardial infarction (R11, R12) could also satisfy 2b but is not needed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: Record R81 (2026-04-09) documents instruction on use and care of the CPAP device by the DME supplier.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test was an attended in-laboratory polysomnography, a Type I facility-based study, which is a permitted sleep test type (R43, R50, R147). The record names the study type but does not document each NCD 240.4.1 validity element separately.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The Type I study results (AHI 14 events/hour with 91 events and Epworth score 17) satisfy the AHI-based criteria in I.B, alternative 2 (see I.B).

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: The attended polysomnography order (R43) was placed by Dr. Irene779 Kirlin939. The same practitioner evaluated the patient in person (R152), documented ordering the sleep study ('Ordered a sleep study'), and reviewed the results (R153).

decision_explanation: All applicable criteria for initial E0601 coverage are met. The in-person evaluation preceded the Type I sleep test. The AHI of 14 with at least 10 events qualifies under alternative 2, supported by documented excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth 17 and dozing while reading and watching television). The treating practitioner ordered the sleep test, and the supplier provided use and care instruction. Sleep Tests.2 and Sleep Tests.5 (FDA status and provider qualification) are administrative and were excluded. Continued-coverage, replacement, oxygen, accessory, humidifier, and billing rules do not apply to this initial device order.
